utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note this headset has been changed recently. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Could the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-03-68-PT, The Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, counsel. For the Prosecution appear Mr. Jayantha Jayasuriya, trial attorney; Mrs. Kimberley Fleming, trial support; and myself, Ekkehard Withopf, acting senior trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Vasija Vidovic, and I'm here with Mr. John Jones to represent Mr. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic. This is the first Status Conference held in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The purpose of having this Status Conference is to organise exchanges between the parties and to review the status of the case so as to ensure the expeditious preparation for trial. Prior to present Status Conference, there have been two Rule 65 ter conferences convened by the Senior Legal Officer of this Chamber. She has kept me well-informed of the conferences, and I would like to comment that the spirit of cooperation demonstrated by both parties is very much welcomed by the Trial Chamber, and I strongly encourage such spirit to continue. And I gather both parties have received the Trial Chamber's decision yesterday regarding the Prosecution's motions for protective measures and delayed disclosure, which motion have been pending for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Therefore, there are no more outstanding motions at this moment. Am I right in that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: It's the understanding of the Prosecution that there are no outstanding motion any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This being said, then let us begin with the disclosure issues. I'm aware that in terms of disclosure of Rule 66(A)(i) materials, it has been basically completed; that is, 49 witness statements accompanied the indictment and confirmation have been disclosed in both English and B/C/S without redaction, except for five statements which have been disclosed in the same redacted format as was provided to the confirming judge. Is there anything the parties wish to comment in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. As of today, we have received the complete material in accordance with the rules. We received this material even earlier. However, some parts of the material were missing so that today the Prosecutor handed over the complete set. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Just for clarification, the Prosecution is of the opinion that the complete set actually has been disclosed within the time limit as prescribed in Rule 66(A)(i); however, based on a letter we received yesterday, we again disclosed binders of the supporting materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I appreciate it. Then Mr. Withopf, in terms of Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure, what is the situation like?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, from the outset, it must be emphasised that the Prosecution disclosed as part of the supporting materials all its currently available witness statements. So in terms of Rule 66(A)(ii), we are talking only about the so-called prior or previous statements. ISU searches have been initiated in May, however to date we got very few results, only due to the fact that this case hasn't been given high priority. Temporarily, this case can be given higher priority. That means that at least a number of such searches can be done in the near future, and we anticipate results within the next four to six weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This matter has something to do with the number of witnesses the Prosecution is to call in the trial stage. And if you have any comments on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: We are currently talking about 49 witnesses. These are the witnesses whose statements form part of the indictment supporting materials. We anticipate some 10, maybe 12 to 15, additional witnesses, and we also anticipate that a few of the already available witness will be reinterviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So all of them are live witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That is not entirely correct. We anticipate that at least at the very minimum, 8 of the 49 currently available witness will be so-called Rule 92 bis witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you can remind me of the meaning of what ISU means.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's the section within the Office of the Prosecutor which runs the keyword based searches for Rule 66(A)(ii) and 68 searches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. So at this moment, you are not in the position to tell when the Prosecution will be able to complete this disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to inform you right now, but it can be anticipated that by the end of this year, we will be in such a position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember the end of this year is the date that the Prosecution suggested to complete -- to file its pre-trial brief. Is it right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will deal with it later when we come to the issue of pre-trial brief. So let's make it clear that at this stage, that the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Prosecution will be able to complete the Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure at the time of the filing of the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: At the very latest. We are talking, and I again emphasise it, only about prior statements, and such statements are very likely to be so-called local statements, meaning in the B/C/S language. There wouldn't be any translation issues involved. And not all of the 49 witnesses have given so-called prior statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And in terms of Rule 68 disclosure of exculpatory material, I understand that this is an ongoing business which has started already. Is there anything you would like to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's entirely correct. It's an ongoing obligation. Again, ISU searches have been initiated in May. The Prosecution is using 96 search criteria for such searches. We are in the very similar situation as in respect to the Rule 66(A)(ii) searches, but we anticipate that most of the material will be available by the end of this year. And again it's an ongoing obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there anything the Defence would like to add on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday at the 65 ter conference, we agreed in detail regarding the Prosecutor's obligation to meet the requirements under Rule 68. We have made certain requests. We will make more specific requests to the Prosecution, and we request that the Prosecutor begins to fulfill this obligation very seriously from several aspects. We discussed this a lot yesterday. In particular because the majority of the relevant archives according to our information are in the possession of the Prosecutor. Until a different decision is made, we request that the Prosecutor makes an effort to submit the evidence to us as soon as possible from the public archives which are in their possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I assume those kind of issues can be resolved through the cooperation of the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Certainly can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then the -- now I turn to expert reports. I believe the Prosecution is anticipating only one such expert, a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's entirely correct, Your Honour. If at all, it will be only one military expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that can be disclosed at the latest at the time of the filing of pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's exactly what we anticipate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's turn to the most important matter. I was informed that the Prosecution has stated that it will be ready to file its pre-trial brief by the end of this year, which means four months from now. Would it not be possible for the Prosecution to shorten the period by any means? For example, by the end of November, which means seven months from the initial appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, we can make efforts to comply with such a deadline. But end of the year would be some sort of more appropriate for the Prosecution. If however, Your Honour wishes us to file such a pre-trial brief by the end of November, we would be in such a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would appreciate it very much because the next Status Conference is to held before the 26th of November. So what I have in mind is I would like to have that Status Conference after the Prosecution's pre-trial brief is filed and before the Defence will file its pre-trial briefs. So that I think it's more convenient to have the Status Conference in that timing. So please, do your -- try your best to provide us with your pre-trial brief by the end of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: We will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having said those, is there anything the parties wish to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Not from the side of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence counsel has nothing to raise either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before I adjourn, I understand that parties have been made aware that this case may become the test case for the Tribunal in utilising a software programme called CaseMap presented by the Prosecution. And there will be a demonstration for the programme sometime in late August. Mr. Withopf, are you in the position to tell us as to what the programme is like and what would be the advantage of using it, in short sentences?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The programme, the so-called CaseMap programme is a programme, it's basically a tool that enables both parties to show the links between the certain events, certain locations, and certain persons. It enables whichever party to very effectively prepare for trial and it's also of very much use in the course of the trial. And it would show the strength and the weaknesses obviously that applies for both sides, and it certainly would help in terms of potential agreement between the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it would be helpful if we could get some brief explanation prior to the demonstration.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The demonstration, as I understand, is scheduled for Wednesday, the 27th of August. And at this point in time, the relevant information can be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, the 27th is a little bit inconvenient. I suggested to my senior legal officer the 28th, so that can be checked. And unless there's anything to be raised -- Mr. Oric, do you have anything to say at this moment? Then this hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.16 p.m.
